messages:
alina: heads-up — saw duplicate token billing after switching a canary to the cost-first routing policy. happened during a flaky network window when clients tried to resume SSE.

alina: minimal repro: start SSE -> drop packets -> client reconnects -> we get two resume attempts within 2s and both billed. proxy logs show old session still considered "resumable" for ~60s (tombstone TTL). snippet:
```
[proxy] recv: resume-id=R123 conn=abc state=stale
[proxy] tombstone created ttl=60s
[proxy] new resume request resume-id=R123 -> allocate new session
billing: charge for tokens from both sessions
```

raj: ugh. i thought we already tombstoned immediately on new resume? sounds like an interaction with sticky routing + cost-first fallback.

maria: i can see traces where resume request went to different region after route flip, old session didn't get tombstone message because route-change path doesn't notify origin. console shows single session in timeline (UI deduped by resume-id) but billing shows two token streams.

kevin: i can reproduce locally if i flip routing during reconnect: route A returns 204 keepalive then client reconnects to route B while A still accepts/resumes. looks like tombstone only happens on explicit session close, not on cross-route takeover.

alina: proposal: on route transfer or when we accept a competing resume, emit a tombstone event to origin and immediately mark previous session as tombstoned (ttl=0) so it refuses further token accounting. also add guard that only one session may be in ACTIVE+ACCEPTED for a resume-id.

raj: agree. small fix in proxy: when we accept a resume from another backend, send an internal /session/tombstone POST to previous backend (best-effort) and set local tombstone flag. fallback: if POST fails, fallback to immediate tombstone locally and emit a metric `session.tombstone.force`.

maria: add telemetry: increment metric when tombstone POST fails and add a new console dashboard panel showing "resume collisions" and charges by resume-id for last 24h. this will help detect canary regressions.

kevin: note: need to be careful with rollout UX. if we immediately tombstone on route changes, canary users might see short reconnect loops if their client tries to resume with stale seq. maybe add a graceful tombstone window of ~3s plus a clear console annotation for canary traffic.

alina: agree — plan: immediate logical tombstone (stop accounting + return 410 to further resumes) but still send a short grace keepalive for clients so they get a terminal and can reconnect cleanly. Console will show "Tombstoned by route-transfer" with link to traces.

maria: i'll create a dashboard PR (grafana) with panels: resume-collisions, tombstone-failures, duplicate-billing-alert rule. can we also emit a structured log with fields: resume_id, old_region, new_region, accepted_at, tombstone_action? makes it easier to wire to console.

raj: i'll do the proxy change and add the metric. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/452

deploy-bot: deploy queued: proxy 0.24.3 -> canary (eng-platform) at 2024-08-02T14:12:00Z

kevin: after deploy let's run chaos test that flips routing during reconnects and verify billing doesn't double-count. also add an integration smoke that asserts only one ACTIVE session per resume-id across regions.

alina: great. assigning follow-ups: raj (proxy fix + metric), maria (dashboard + alerts), kevin (chaos + integration test). i'll update rollout checklist to include "resume collision" smoke. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
